name: Should I choose a single-handle or two-handle kitchen faucet?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a single-handle or two-handle kitchen faucet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Single-handle faucets offer convenience, letting you adjust temperature and water flow with one hand, which is ideal when cooking. Two-handle faucets provide precise separate control of hot and cold water and fit traditional decor. The tradeoff is installation complexity: single-handle faucets typically use a single hole (with an optional escutcheon plate), whereas two-handle designs require three holes spaced specifically. Selecting a model that matches your current sink drillings avoids the need for drilling extra holes in stone surfaces.
acceptedAnswer.description: Single-handle faucets provide quick one-handed temperature adjustments, while two-handle models offer precise control but require multiple holes.
